description: The Pyrenean Digital Climate Atlas, produced by CREAF and the GRUMETS research group with CSIC participation, provides terrain-adjusted climate maps for the Pyrenees. Meteorological station observations, altitude, latitude, distance from the sea and potential solar radiation were combined through geostatistical modelling for 1950–2012. Monthly, seasonal and annual layers include minimum, mean and maximum temperature, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, water availability, growing degree-days and potential solar radiation. Zenodo supplies GeoTIFF archives with ISO 19139 XML metadata free under CC-BY-4.0. These maps can provide baseline conditions for mountain water-balance, irrigation-demand and renewable-energy simulations. Derived evapotranspiration and water availability complement the temperature and precipitation layers within the same collection. They are long-term climatic products, not a daily sequence for storm replay. Grid spacing is unknown from the inspected repository description, and the Thornthwaite-derived variables inherit the assumptions of that method.
